name: 3M
title: 3M Peltor Optime III & Helmet Earmuffs
meta: 3M Peltor hearing protection for tree crews, including the Optime III earmuff and helmet-mount muffs that keep saw noise down on long cutting days.
intro: 3M makes the Peltor hearing protection a lot of tree crews wear under and on their helmets. The 3M Peltor Optime III is the high-attenuation muff people reach for when they run big saws, chippers and stump grinders all day.
about: Most tree work is loud work. A pro chainsaw, a chipper and a stump grinder will all push you past safe exposure long before lunch, and hearing damage does not come back. 3M's Peltor line is one of the most common answers on the job: headband muffs for ground crews, helmet-mount muffs that clip into the slots on many arborist helmets, and foam plugs for anyone who prefers them.

The Optime family comes in a few levels of attenuation, with the Optime III at the heavy end for high-noise equipment. Helmet-mount versions let you flip the cups up when you are talking through a cut and snap them back down when the saw starts. If you run a radio setup, check fit and compatibility with your helmet before you buy, and replace ear cushions when they harden or crack, since a poor seal costs you protection.
known_for: Protection for saw, chipper and grinder noise

name: All Gear
title: All Gear Rope, Slings & Rigging Gear
meta: All Gear rope and rigging gear for tree work: climbing lines, loggers rope, bull rope, slings and lanyards built for daily use by climbers and ground crews.
intro: All Gear is a familiar name in arborist rope and rigging. Crews know All Gear for practical climbing lines, rigging rope, loggers rope, slings and lanyards that hold up to daily work.
about: All Gear focuses on the soft goods that get used and abused on every job: ropes for climbing and rigging, loggers rope, slings, and pre-made lanyards. It tends to suit crews who want straightforward, working-grade gear rather than boutique colors and features.

Rigging lines, loggers rope and bull rope from All Gear show up on removal crews that go through a lot of rope. As with any line, match the rope to the load and the hardware it runs through, check the manufacturer's breaking strength, and retire rope that is glazed, cut, cored or shock-loaded. Life-support rope should meet ANSI Z133 requirements and be inspected before every climb.

name: Alliance Equipment
title: Alliance Equipment Tree Care Gear
meta: Alliance Equipment gear for tree care crews. Browse the Alliance Equipment items we carry, with plain notes on how each piece is used on the job.
intro: Alliance Equipment is a brand you will find on a handful of tree care and jobsite products. This page collects the Alliance Equipment items we list, with honest notes on what each one is for.
about: We keep brand pages like this one simple: rather than make claims about a company we cannot verify, we let the products speak for themselves. Each Alliance Equipment listing covers what the item does, where it fits on a tree job, and what to check before you buy.

If you are comparing Alliance Equipment gear against other options, look at the basics first: rated strength for anything that holds a load, materials and build quality, and whether it fits the rest of your kit. For any life-support or rigging use, follow the manufacturer's instructions and the applicable ANSI Z133 requirements.

name: Arbortec
title: Arbortec Chainsaw Pants & Arborist Clothing
meta: Arbortec chainsaw pants and arborist clothing from the UK. Compare Arbortec chainsaw trousers, Breatheflex pants and suspenders for climbers and ground crews.
intro: Arbortec is a British brand that makes chainsaw pants, jackets and work clothing built around how arborists move. Arbortec chainsaw trousers are popular with climbers who want protection without feeling like they are wearing armor.
about: Arbortec started in the UK, where chainsaw trousers are the norm rather than chaps, and that shows in the design. Their chainsaw pants are cut for climbing and kneeling, with stretch panels, venting and protective layers built into the front of the legs. The Breatheflex line is the one most climbers ask about, aimed at warm days and lots of movement.

Beyond pants, Arbortec makes work shirts, jackets, base layers and accessories like heavy-duty suspenders for chainsaw pants. If you run a saw in the tree or spend all day on the ground bucking, chainsaw pants can be more comfortable than strapping on chaps. Check the protection rating on the label against what your employer and the applicable standard require.

name: Arborwear
title: Arborwear Pants & Tree Climber Clothing
meta: Arborwear pants and work clothing made for tree climbers. Tough double-layer pants, shirts and outerwear from the Arborwear line for real tree work.
intro: Arborwear makes work clothing that started with tree climbers in mind. Arborwear pants are known for heavy canvas, reinforced knees and a gusseted crotch that lets you step high in a saddle.
about: Arborwear is a US company whose clothing grew out of the needs of working climbers. Their tree climbers' pants are built from heavy cotton canvas with doubled fabric where bark and rope wear through first, and a cut that does not bind when you throw a leg over a limb or step up on a spur.

The line has spread to shirts, flannels, jackets, hats and lighter pants for warm weather, but pants are still what most people come for. Arborwear pants are not chainsaw protective by themselves, so pair them with chaps on the ground or choose dedicated chainsaw pants when the job calls for them.

name: ArbPro
title: ArbPro Arborist Gear
meta: ArbPro arborist gear for climbers and ground crews. See the ArbPro items we carry and what each one does on a tree job, explained in plain language.
intro: ArbPro is a name you will see on a small range of arborist gear. This page gathers the ArbPro products we list so you can compare them side by side with other brands.
about: We do not pad brand pages with marketing claims. Each ArbPro listing explains the item, how it gets used on a climb or on the ground, and what to check before you put it into service.

If any ArbPro item is part of your life-support or rigging system, read and follow the manufacturer's instructions, confirm its ratings, and inspect it before each use. Gear that holds a person or a load should meet the applicable ANSI Z133 requirements and be used by trained workers.
known_for: Gear for climbers and ground crews

name: ARS
title: ARS Pruning Tools: Japanese Pruners & Saws
meta: ARS pruning tools from Japan: hand pruners, pole pruners and pruning saws with hard, sharp blades. A good fit for detail pruning, orchards and landscape work.
intro: ARS is a Japanese maker of pruning tools, including hand pruners, pole pruners and pruning saws. ARS pruning tools are known for hard, sharp blades and light weight, which makes them popular for detail pruning and orchard work.
about: ARS tools come out of the Japanese tradition of fine-edged, lightweight cutting tools. Their hand pruners are slim and quick, with blades that take and hold a very sharp edge, and they show up a lot in orchards, vineyards and landscape maintenance as well as in arborist kits.

Their pole pruners and pruning saws suit climbers and ground crews doing structural and detail pruning on smaller wood, where clean cuts matter more than brute force. Keep blades clean and lightly oiled, and replace worn blades rather than forcing a dull tool through a cut.

name: ART
title: ART SpiderJack, Positioner & Climbing Gear
meta: ART (Arbor Rope Technologies) climbing gear, including the SpiderJack friction device, Positioner 2 swivel lanyard adjuster and Ropeguide friction saver.
intro: ART, short for Arbor Rope Technologies, makes engineered climbing hardware for arborists. The ART SpiderJack is its best-known piece, alongside the Positioner lanyard adjuster and the Ropeguide friction saver.
about: ART designs gear for climbers who like mechanical solutions. The SpiderJack is a mechanical friction device that takes the place of a friction hitch on a moving rope system, giving consistent, adjustable friction and smooth tending. The Positioner, including the Positioner 2 with swivel, is a lanyard adjuster designed for work positioning.

ART also makes the Ropeguide, a friction saver that protects both the tree and your line at the tie-in point. This kind of hardware rewards climbers who read the instructions closely and practice low and slow before using it at height. Learn it with a qualified trainer, follow ART's instructions for compatible ropes and connectors, and inspect it before every climb.

name: Buckingham
title: Buckingham Gaffs, Spurs & Climbing Saddles
meta: Buckingham gaffs, climbing spurs and saddles for tree and line work. Compare Buckingham steel climbers, BuckAlloy gaffs, Big Buck pads and replacement parts.
intro: Buckingham is a long-running US maker of climbing spurs, gaffs, saddles and lineman gear. Buckingham gaffs and steel climbers are a common sight on removal crews.
about: Buckingham builds climbing equipment in the United States for tree workers and utility linemen. Their steel climbers are a removal-crew standard, sold with different pad options such as Big Buck pads and T-pads, and their BuckAlloy replacement gaffs are a common upgrade or replacement when original gaffs are worn.

Buckingham also makes climbing saddles, positioning lanyards and parts. Remember that spurs are for removals and emergency access only, not for pruning live trees. Keep gaffs sharp to the manufacturer's profile, check straps and pads for wear, and get trained before climbing on spurs.
known_for: Big Buck and T-pad climber pads

name: CAMP
title: CAMP Climbing Gear, Harnesses & Carabiners
meta: CAMP climbing gear from Italy for tree work and rope access: harnesses, carabiners, helmets and descenders. Compare CAMP Safety gear before your next climb.
intro: CAMP is an Italian climbing gear maker whose CAMP Safety line covers harnesses, carabiners, helmets and devices for work at height. CAMP climbing gear shows up in arborist, rope access and rescue kits.
about: CAMP has a long history in mountaineering and climbing, and its CAMP Safety division builds gear for professional work at height. For tree workers that means harnesses, connectors, helmets, pulleys and descenders that cross over well from rope access and rescue.

If you are looking at a CAMP harness or device for arborist use, check that it is rated for the way you will use it and compatible with your rope diameter and connectors. Read the instructions, train with a qualified person, and inspect life-support gear before every use.

name: Climb Right
title: Climb Right Climbing Spurs & Climbers
meta: Climb Right climbing spurs for tree removal work, including aluminum climbers with Big Buck or steel support pads. Lightweight spurs for crews on removals.
intro: Climb Right makes climbing spurs for tree work, including aluminum climbers that cut weight on long removal days. Climb Right spurs are offered with different pad options to suit how you climb.
about: Lighter spurs mean less fatigue when you spend the day climbing removals. Climb Right aluminum climbers are aimed at that use, paired with pads such as Big Buck pads or steel support pads to spread the load across your lower leg.

Spurs damage living tissue, so keep them for removals and emergency access, not pruning. Fit matters: the shank length, pad and straps should match your leg. Keep gaffs sharp, replace worn straps, and learn spur climbing with a qualified trainer.

name: Climbing Innovations
title: Climbing Innovations: Haas Ascenders & Gear
meta: Climbing Innovations gear for arborists, including the Haas knee ascender system, Haas Velox and ascent accessories for faster, easier rope climbing.
intro: Climbing Innovations makes gear that helps arborists get up the rope with less effort. It is best known for the Haas knee ascender system and related ascent accessories.
about: Ascending a rope is where a lot of climbers burn energy before the work even starts. Climbing Innovations focuses on that part of the climb, with the Haas knee ascender system and the Haas Velox, which let you use your legs in a more natural stepping motion on a single rope.

Systems like these work best when they are set up to fit your body and practiced low to the ground first. Follow the manufacturer's setup instructions, use them with compatible ropes and devices, and get training before relying on any new ascent system at height.

name: Climbing Technology
title: Climbing Technology Carabiners & Gear
meta: Climbing Technology gear from Italy for arborists: carabiners, ascenders, harnesses and rigging hardware. Plain notes on each piece and how crews use it.
intro: Climbing Technology is an Italian maker of climbing and work-at-height equipment. Arborists use Climbing Technology carabiners, ascenders, pulleys and harnesses in both climbing and rigging setups.
about: Climbing Technology, often shortened to CT, builds a wide range of connectors and devices for mountaineering, rope access and tree work. The range covers aluminum and steel carabiners, rope clamps and ascenders, pulleys and harnesses.

For tree workers, CT hardware fits in wherever you need a dependable connector or device that plays well with the rest of your system. Check every item's rating and rope compatibility, follow the instructions, and inspect life-support gear before use.

name: Corona
title: Corona Tree Pruners, Loppers & Pole Saws
meta: Corona tree pruners, loppers, pole saws and replacement parts. Practical Corona cutting tools for landscape crews, orchard work and homeowners alike.
intro: Corona is a US maker of hand pruners, loppers, pole saws and pruning tools. Corona tree pruners and their replacement parts are a common pick for landscape crews and property maintenance.
about: Corona tools are built for steady, everyday pruning. Their line runs from hand pruners and loppers to pole pruners and pole saws, which makes them a good fit for landscape maintenance, orchards and ground-based pruning on smaller trees.

A big plus is that many Corona tools have replaceable blades, springs and parts, so a worn tool can often be brought back instead of thrown out. Keep blades sharp and clean, and use a pole pruner only well clear of power lines.

name: Courant
title: Courant Rope, Koala Harness & Rope Bags
meta: Courant rope, the Koala climbing harness and Courant rope bags for arborists. French climbing gear for tree workers who want a well-sorted kit.
intro: Courant is a French maker of rope and climbing gear for arborists. Courant rope, the Koala harness and Courant rope bags all have a following among climbers.
about: Courant comes from rope making, and its climbing lines and accessory cords are the base of the range. On top of that sits arborist-specific gear like the Koala harness and a line of rope bags that keep your climbing line clean and organized between climbs.

As with any life-support gear, check that rope diameter and construction match the devices and hitches you use, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and inspect your rope and harness before every climb.

name: Distel
title: Distel Climbing Spurs & Replacement Parts
meta: Distel climbing spurs and replacement parts, including pads with rings and straps. Gear for tree removal climbers who want to keep their spurs in service.
intro: Distel makes climbing spurs and spur parts for tree workers. Distel replacement pads, rings and straps help you keep a set of climbers in good working shape.
about: Spurs take a beating on removal work, and the pads and straps wear out long before the shanks. Distel offers climbers along with replacement pads that come with rings and straps, so you can refresh the parts that touch your leg.
Use spurs only for removals or emergency access. Check strap stitching and buckles before each climb, keep gaffs sharpened to the correct profile, and replace parts that are cracked, frayed or worn.
known_for: Replacement pads with rings and straps

name: DMM
title: DMM Climbing Carabiners, Pulleys & Swivels
meta: DMM climbing hardware from Wales: carabiners, pulleys, swivels and rigging gear arborists trust. Compare DMM connectors like the Shadow and XSRE carabiners.
intro: DMM is a Welsh maker of climbing hardware known for forged carabiners, pulleys and swivels. DMM climbing gear is a staple in arborist climbing and rigging kits.
about: DMM forges its hardware in North Wales and has a reputation for clean, well-finished connectors. Arborists use DMM carabiners on their bridges, lanyards and pulleys, from auto-locking models like the Shadow to small accessory biners for hanging gear.

Beyond carabiners, DMM makes pulleys, swivels and rigging hardware that sees a lot of use in both climbing systems and lowering setups. Choose the gate type and rating for the job, keep connectors loaded along the spine, and retire any hardware that has been dropped hard onto a hard surface or shows cracks or deep grooves.

name: Eagle Safety
title: Eagle Safety Gear for Tree Crews
meta: Eagle Safety gear for tree crews and jobsites. See the Eagle Safety items we carry, with practical notes on how each piece fits into a safe day of work.
intro: Eagle Safety is a brand you will find on a range of safety products. This page collects the Eagle Safety items we list, with straightforward notes on what each one is for.
about: We keep this page focused on the products. Each Eagle Safety listing covers what the item does, where it fits on a tree job, and what to check before using it.

Safety gear only works if it fits, is rated for the hazard and is actually worn. Match each item to the task, check any certification on the label, and replace gear that is damaged or past its service life.

name: Echo
title: Echo Chainsaws, Pole Saws & Chainsaw Chaps
meta: Echo chainsaw chaps, chainsaws, pole saws and power equipment for tree work. Compare Echo saws and protective gear for ground crews and climbers.
intro: Echo makes outdoor power equipment including chainsaws, top-handle saws, pole saws and blowers, plus protective gear like chainsaw chaps. Echo gear is common on landscape and tree crews.
about: Echo is a Japanese-origin power equipment brand with a big presence in professional landscape and tree care. Their lineup covers rear-handle and top-handle chainsaws, pole saws, trimmers and blowers, and the gear that goes with them.

Echo chainsaw chaps are a simple way to add leg protection when you are running a saw on the ground. Whatever saw or chaps you run, read the operator's manual, wear the full set of PPE, and get trained before you cut.

name: Edelrid
title: Edelrid Talon, TreeRex & Climbing Gear
meta: Edelrid climbing gear from Germany for arborists: the Talon spur upper strap system, TreeRex harness, chest harness, ropes and carabiners for tree work.
intro: Edelrid is a German climbing gear maker with a strong arborist range. The Edelrid Talon spur system and the TreeRex harness are two of its best-known tree work products.
about: Edelrid has deep roots in climbing rope and hardware, and its tree care line builds on that. The TreeRex harness and its bungee chest harness are aimed at climbers who want a modular, adjustable setup, and Edelrid also makes ropes, carabiners and accessories.

The Talon is Edelrid's take on climbing spurs, with an upper strap system designed to hold the spur securely and spread pressure. Use spurs for removals only, set up the straps to fit your leg, and follow the manufacturer's instructions for any life-support gear.
known_for: Talon spur and upper strap system

name: Fanno
title: Fanno Saw Works Pruning Saws & Blades
meta: Fanno Saw Works pruning saws and replacement blades for arborists, orchardists and landscape crews. Durable hand saws and pole saw blades for daily pruning.
intro: Fanno Saw Works makes pruning saws and pole saw blades used by arborists, orchard crews and landscapers. Fanno saws are known as tough, no-nonsense cutting tools.
about: Fanno Saw Works builds hand saws and pole saw blades in the United States. Their saws are made for the steady pruning work of orchards and tree crews, with blades in different lengths and tooth patterns and replacement blades that keep a handle in service for years.

A Fanno pole saw blade on a good pole is still one of the quickest ways to reach small limbs from the ground. Keep blades clean, store them in a scabbard, and stay well clear of power lines when using any pole tool.

name: Felco
title: Felco Pruners: Felco 2, 12 & Pruning Kits
meta: Felco pruners from Switzerland, including the Felco 2, Felco 12 and Felco 5, plus kits and spare parts. Precise hand pruners for arborists and landscapers.
intro: Felco is the Swiss maker of hand pruners that many arborists and landscapers carry every day. The Felco 2 is the classic, and the Felco 12 is a popular compact option for smaller hands.
about: Felco pruners are built to be used hard and repaired rather than replaced. Blades, springs and other parts can be swapped as they wear, so a good pair can last for a very long time with sharpening and care.

The Felco 2 is the standard full-size model, the Felco 12 suits smaller hands, and the Felco 5 is a more basic option. Kits bundle a pruner with a holster or sharpener. Clean sap off the blades after use and keep the edge sharp for cuts that close well.

name: Forester
title: Forester Chainsaw Tools & Accessories
meta: Forester tools and chainsaw accessories for tree crews and woodcutters: files, wedges, chaps and jobsite gear at working-crew prices, with plain-spoken notes.
intro: Forester is a brand of chainsaw accessories and woodcutting tools. Forester tools tend to be budget-friendly basics that fill out a saw kit.
about: Forester covers the everyday items around the saw: filing gear, wedges, protective gear and jobsite accessories. It suits crews and woodcutters who need functional gear without paying top dollar for every piece.

For protective gear, check the label for the standard and protection level it meets. For tools, buy what fits your saw and your chain. Replace worn files and damaged wedges, and inspect PPE before each use.

name: FTC
title: FTC Climbing Gear for Arborists
meta: FTC climbing gear for arborists. See the FTC items we list, with plain notes on what each piece does and how it fits into a tree climbing setup.
intro: FTC is a name you will find on a small range of tree climbing gear. This page gathers the FTC items we list so you can see what each one does.
about: Rather than make claims about a brand we cannot fully verify, we let the listings speak for themselves. Each FTC product page explains the item, how it is used in the tree, and what to check before you buy.

If an FTC item is part of your climbing system, follow the manufacturer's instructions, confirm its ratings and rope compatibility, and inspect it before every climb. Life-support gear should meet the applicable ANSI Z133 requirements and be used by trained climbers.

name: Good Rigging
title: Good Rigging Control System (GRCS)
meta: The Good Rigging Control System (GRCS) is a portable capstan winch for tree rigging. Learn what the GRCS does, how crews use it and what to consider.
intro: Good Rigging is best known for the Good Rigging Control System, or GRCS, a portable winch and lowering device that mounts to the tree. Crews use the GRCS to lift, pull and lower heavy pieces with more control.
about: The GRCS combines a capstan winch with a lowering device in one unit that straps to the trunk. That lets a ground crew pretension a rigging line, pull over tops, lift wood out of tight spots and then lower it under control, all with the same setup.

It is a big step up for removal crews that handle heavy wood in tight yards. Rigging forces can be far higher than people expect, so size ropes, slings and blocks for the loads, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure operators are trained.

name: Green Manufacturing
title: Green Manufacturing Tree Care Tools
meta: Green Manufacturing tools for tree care and landscape crews. See the Green Manufacturing items we carry, with plain notes on what each one does on the job.
intro: Green Manufacturing is a name you will see on a small range of tree care and landscape tools. This page collects the Green Manufacturing products we list.
about: We keep brand pages honest and focused on the gear. Each Green Manufacturing listing explains what the tool is for, how it fits into tree care or landscape work, and what to look for before you buy.
As with any tool, use it for the job it was designed for, keep it clean and in good repair, and replace it when it is worn or damaged.

name: Hasegawa
title: Hasegawa Ladders for Tree & Orchard Work
meta: Hasegawa ladders for tree care, orchard and landscape pruning work. Learn what to look for in a ladder for pruning, and how to set one up safely on the ground.
intro: Hasegawa is a ladder brand. Hasegawa ladders are used by crews who prune from the ground up and need a stable platform in the yard or orchard.
about: A good ladder still has a place in tree work, especially for hedge, orchard and small-tree pruning where climbing gear is overkill. Hasegawa ladders are made for that kind of work, with designs meant to stand on uneven ground.
Set any ladder on firm footing, check the rated load, and never lean it against a limb you are about to cut. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and keep three points of contact.

name: Irwin
title: Irwin Hand Tools for Tree Crews
meta: Irwin hand tools for tree crews and jobsites: wrenches, clamps, saws and other basics for the truck. Practical tools with plain notes on how crews use them.
intro: Irwin makes hand tools that end up in a lot of work trucks. Tree crews use Irwin tools for maintenance, repairs and the small jobs that come up around the saws and equipment.
about: Irwin is a well-known hand tool brand covering wrenches, pliers, clamps, saws, bits and more. On a tree crew those tools handle truck and chipper maintenance, hardware swaps and quick fixes on the jobsite.
Keep a basic tool roll on the truck and you will save a lot of downtime. Use the right size tool for each fastener, and replace tools that are cracked or worn.

name: ISC
title: ISC Rope Wrench, Pulleys & Rigging Gear
meta: ISC climbing equipment from Wales for arborists: the ISC Rope Wrench, pulleys, rigging blocks and hardware for climbing and lowering systems.
intro: ISC is a Welsh maker of climbing and rigging hardware for arborists and rope access. The ISC Rope Wrench helped make stationary rope climbing popular in tree care.
about: ISC builds pulleys, rigging blocks, rope grabs and connectors used by tree workers around the world. Its Rope Wrench pairs with a friction hitch to make single rope climbing in trees practical, and it remains a common first SRS device.

On the rigging side, ISC blocks and pulleys are used for lowering and redirecting loads. Size every piece of rigging hardware for the forces involved, follow the instructions, and train with a qualified person before using any new climbing system at height.

name: Jameson
title: Jameson Pole Tools, Pruners & Rope Sniper
meta: Jameson tools for tree work: pole saws, tree pruners, fiberglass poles, throw line gear and the Rope Sniper tool for setting lines from the ground.
intro: Jameson makes pole tools, tree pruners and line placement gear for arborists and utility crews. Jameson tools are known for durable fiberglass poles and practical pruning heads.
about: Jameson's core line is pole tools: fiberglass poles, pole saws and pruner heads that work together as a system. Ground crews use them to reach small limbs, clear deadwood and handle work near structures without climbing.

The Rope Sniper is a pole-mounted tool for placing a line over a limb without a throw bag. Even with fiberglass poles, keep all pole tools well away from energized lines and follow utility clearance rules.

name: K&H Distributing
title: K&H Felling Wedges
meta: K&H felling wedges for tree felling and bucking. Plastic wedges that help set direction and keep the bar from getting pinched, with sizes for different saws.
intro: K&H Distributing is known for felling wedges. K&H felling wedges help keep a cut open and guide trees over during felling and bucking.
about: Wedges are cheap insurance on the ground. They keep the kerf open so the bar does not pinch, and they help lift a tree over in the direction you want during felling. K&H wedges come in different lengths and heights to match bar size and wood.
Use plastic wedges, never steel, around a running chain. Carry more than one, check them for cracks and mushroomed heads, and get trained in felling before relying on wedges to control a tree.

name: Kask
title: Kask Arborist Helmets & Replacement Parts
meta: Kask arborist helmets from Italy, like the Super Plasma, plus replacement parts, chin straps, visors and earmuff adapters for climbing and chainsaw work.
intro: Kask is an Italian helmet maker whose arborist helmets are a common sight in trees. Kask arborist helmets like the Super Plasma are known for comfort, venting and a wide range of accessories.
about: Kask builds helmets for climbing, work at height and chainsaw use. The Super Plasma is one of the most popular in tree care, with a comfortable fit system, good venting and slots for visors and hearing protection.

A big reason crews stick with Kask is parts support: replacement chin straps, pads, visors and adapters keep a helmet in service and comfortable. Check helmet ratings for the work you do, replace any helmet after a significant impact, and follow the maker's service-life guidance.

name: Klein
title: Klein Tree Climbing Spikes & Gaffs
meta: Klein tree climbing spikes, gaffs and climbing gear for tree and line work. Compare Klein climbers and replacement gaffs used by utility and tree crews.
intro: Klein Tools is a US tool maker with a long history in utility work. Klein tree climbing spikes and gaffs are used by both linemen and tree removal crews.
about: Klein is best known for electrician and lineman tools, and its climbing gear comes out of that utility background. Klein climbers and gaffs are built for durability, with tree gaffs for bark and pole gaffs for utility poles.
Use tree gaffs, not pole gaffs, when climbing trees. Keep spurs for removals and emergencies, keep gaffs sharp to the correct profile, and get trained before climbing on spurs.

name: Kong
title: Kong Climbing Gear: Duck Rope Clamp & Carabiners
meta: Kong climbing gear from Italy for arborists and rope access: the Duck rope clamp, carabiners, pulleys and rescue hardware for climbing and rigging systems.
intro: Kong is an Italian maker of climbing and rescue hardware. Kong climbing gear like the Duck rope clamp and Kong carabiners appear in a lot of arborist and rope access kits.
about: Kong builds connectors, rope clamps, pulleys and devices for climbing, rescue and industrial work. The Duck is a compact rope clamp that climbers use in ascent setups and haul systems, and Kong carabiners come in many shapes and gate styles.

As with any hardware, choose items rated for your use and compatible with your rope, read the instructions, and inspect gear before each use. Hardware that has taken a hard fall onto rock or concrete should be retired.

name: LogRite
title: LogRite Log Arch, Cant Hooks & Peaveys
meta: LogRite log arches, cant hooks and peaveys for moving and rolling logs. The LogRite arch and junior arch make it easier to skid wood without heavy equipment.
intro: LogRite makes log handling tools including log arches, cant hooks and peaveys. A LogRite arch lets one or two people lift the end of a log and roll it out on wheels.
about: Moving wood by hand is slow and hard on your back. LogRite tools give you leverage: cant hooks and peaveys to roll and turn logs, and log arches that pick up one end so you can wheel a log across a yard or trail instead of dragging it.
The junior arch suits smaller logs and tight spaces, while larger arches handle bigger wood. Work on stable ground, keep your feet clear of the log's path, and do not overload any tool.

name: Marlow
title: Marlow Rope for Arborists
meta: Marlow rope from the UK for arborists: climbing lines, rigging rope and accessory cord. Learn how to pick Marlow rope for your climbing system and hardware.
intro: Marlow is a UK rope maker with a range of lines for climbing, rigging and marine use. Marlow rope is used by arborists who want well-made lines with consistent handling.
about: Marlow has a long history in rope making and supplies lines for sailing, industry and tree care. Its arborist range covers climbing ropes, rigging lines and small accessory cords used for prusiks, tool lanyards and other jobs.

Small-diameter Marlow cord can be useful for accessories, but anything that is part of your life-support system must be rated for that use. Match rope diameter to your devices, check minimum breaking strength, and retire rope that shows damage.

name: Marvin
title: Marvin Pole Saw & Pole Pruner Heads
meta: Marvin pole saw heads and pole pruner heads for tree crews. Cast saw heads, bull pruner heads and replacement parts that fit standard pole systems.
intro: Marvin makes pole saw heads and pole pruner heads used by tree and utility crews. Marvin pole pruners and saw heads are a common choice for building a dependable pole tool setup.
about: Marvin focuses on the business end of pole tools. Their pruner heads, including bull pruner heads with pulleys, and cast saw heads mount to poles to reach limbs from the ground or from the tree.
Replacement blades and parts keep heads in service as they wear. Choose a head that fits your pole system, keep blades sharp, and keep all pole tools well away from energized lines.

name: Notch
title: Notch Equipment: Rope Runner Pro, Harnesses & Gear
meta: Notch Equipment climbing gear for arborists: the Rope Runner Pro, Sentinel harness, Flow rope wrench, Quickie hardware and more for tree climbers.
intro: Notch Equipment makes climbing and rigging gear designed for arborists. The Notch Rope Runner Pro and Notch climbing harnesses are some of the best-known products in the range.
about: Notch covers a lot of the tree climber's kit: harnesses such as the Sentinel, mechanical devices like the Rope Runner Pro, the Flow adjustable rope wrench, and small hardware like the Quickie. It also makes throw line gear, slings, lanyards and rigging accessories.

The Rope Runner Pro is a mechanical device for SRS climbing that gives smooth descents and easy tending once it is set up properly. Like any life-support device, it should be learned with a qualified trainer and used per the instructions with compatible ropes.

name: Oregon
title: Oregon Saw Chain, Bars & Files
meta: Oregon saw chain, guide bars, files and sharpening gear for chainsaws. Compare Oregon chain and bars for felling, bucking and climbing saws on tree crews.
intro: Oregon is a US maker of saw chain, guide bars and sharpening tools. Oregon saw chain and bars fit a wide range of chainsaws used in tree work.
about: Chain and bars wear out much faster than the saw, so most crews buy them often. Oregon makes chain in common pitches and gauges, guide bars for a wide range of saws, and the files and guides used to keep chain cutting.

Match chain pitch, gauge and drive link count to your bar, and check your saw's manual for approved combinations. A sharp chain is a safe chain: it cuts with less force and reduces kickback risk compared to a dull one.

name: Petzl
title: Petzl Arborist Gear: Sequoia, ZigZag & More
meta: Petzl arborist gear from France: the Sequoia harness, ZigZag, Vertex helmet, Micrograb, Zillon lanyard and carabiners for tree climbers and riggers.
intro: Petzl is a French maker of climbing and work-at-height gear with a deep arborist range. Petzl gear like the Sequoia harness, ZigZag and Vertex helmet are in kits all over the world.
about: Petzl builds complete climbing systems for tree care: harnesses such as the Sequoia, mechanical friction devices like the ZigZag, lanyards like the Zillon, rope adjusters like the Micrograb, helmets like the Vertex, and a long list of carabiners including the AmD, William and Mino.

Petzl publishes detailed instructions and technical notes for its gear, and they are worth reading. Use compatible ropes and connectors, inspect your gear before every climb, and train with a qualified person before using a new device at height.

name: Pfanner
title: Pfanner Protos Helmet & Parts
meta: Pfanner Protos Integral helmets from Austria, plus replacement parts and accessories. A helmet system with built-in hearing and face protection for saw work.
intro: Pfanner is an Austrian company best known for the Protos Integral helmet system. The Pfanner Protos combines a helmet, visor and hearing protection in one design.
about: The Protos is popular with arborists and forestry workers because everything is integrated: the visor and earmuffs are part of the system, so they work together and stay out of the way when you do not need them. Pfanner also makes chainsaw pants and work clothing.
Replacement parts and accessories keep a Protos helmet in service. Replace worn ear cushions, damaged visors and the helmet itself according to Pfanner's instructions or after any significant impact.

name: Pferd
title: Pferd Chainsaw Files & File Sets
meta: Pferd files and file sets from Germany for chainsaw sharpening. Round files, flat files, depth gauges and file holders for keeping saw chain cutting well.
intro: Pferd is a German tool maker known for high-quality files. Pferd chainsaw files and file sets are a go-to for crews who sharpen in the field.
about: Field sharpening is a skill every saw user should have, and good files make it easier. Pferd makes round files sized for common chain pitches, flat files for depth gauges, and holders and guides that help you hold a consistent angle.
Use the file size your chain maker specifies, file in one direction, and keep cutters even in length. Replace files when they start to skate instead of cut.
known_for: Flat files and depth gauge tools

name: Pro-Climb
title: Pro-Climb Carabiners & Climbing Hardware
meta: Pro-Climb carabiners and climbing hardware for tree work. See the Pro-Climb items we list, with practical notes on how each one fits into a climbing system.
intro: Pro-Climb is a name found on climbing hardware such as carabiners. This page collects the Pro-Climb items we list with plain notes on each.
about: We focus on the gear rather than marketing claims. Each Pro-Climb listing covers the item's role, how it is used in a climbing or rigging setup, and what to check before you put it into service.
For any connector or device used in life support, confirm its rating and gate type, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and inspect it before every use.

name: Pull'R
title: Pull'R Tree Care Gear
meta: Pull'R gear for tree care crews. See the Pull'R products we list, with plain notes on what each item does and how it fits into a jobsite or rigging setup.
intro: Pull'R is a brand found on a small range of jobsite and tree care products. This page collects the Pull'R items we list.
about: We keep this page focused on the products. Each Pull'R listing explains what the item is for, how it fits into tree work, and what to look for before you buy.
For any gear that pulls or holds a load, check its rated capacity, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and inspect it before use.

name: Rock Exotica
title: Rock Exotica Pulleys, Carabiners & Rigging
meta: Rock Exotica hardware for arborists: pulleys, carabiners, swivels and rigging devices like the Downrigger. Well-machined gear for climbing and rigging.
intro: Rock Exotica is a US maker of carabiners, pulleys and rigging hardware. Rock Exotica gear is known for careful machining and smart designs, from the RockX carabiner to rigging devices like the Downrigger.
about: Rock Exotica builds hardware for rescue, rope access and tree care. Arborists use their pulleys and swivels in climbing systems, their carabiners as everyday connectors, and devices like the Downrigger in rigging setups.
Machined, well-finished hardware is easier on rope and runs smoother. Still, size each piece for the forces you will put on it, follow the instructions, and inspect it before every use.

name: SafeTree Products
title: SafeTree Products for Tree Crews
meta: SafeTree Products gear for tree crews, including the Safe-T Stepper. See the SafeTree items we list, with plain notes on how each one is used on the job.
intro: SafeTree Products is a small brand with a few items aimed at tree work. This page gathers the SafeTree products we list, including the Safe-T Stepper.
about: We keep this page simple and focused on what each product does. Each SafeTree listing covers the item, how it is used on a tree job, and what to check before you buy.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions, check ratings, and inspect any gear that supports your weight before using it.

name: Safewaze
title: Safewaze Fall Protection & Safety Harnesses
meta: Safewaze fall protection for jobsites and bucket work: full-body safety harnesses, lanyards and self-retracting lifelines. Learn what to check before buying.
intro: Safewaze is a US fall protection brand. Safewaze safety harnesses, lanyards and self-retracting lifelines are used on construction sites and in aerial lift work.
about: Fall protection is its own world, separate from arborist climbing gear. Safewaze makes full-body harnesses, shock-absorbing lanyards and self-retracting lifelines for workers who need fall arrest, such as in aerial lifts and on rooftops.

A fall arrest harness is not a climbing saddle, and the two are not interchangeable. Use the gear that matches the task, follow the manufacturer's instructions and your employer's fall protection plan, and inspect before each use.

name: Samson Rope
title: Samson Ropes: Climbing, Rigging & Throw Line
meta: Samson ropes for arborists: climbing lines, rigging rope like Stable Braid and Tenex, and Zing-It throw line. Compare Samson rope for your climbing system.
intro: Samson is a US rope maker with one of the widest arborist rope ranges around. Samson ropes cover climbing lines, rigging lines and the Zing-It throw line.
about: Samson makes rope for marine, industrial and tree care work. For arborists that means climbing lines in different constructions and diameters, double-braid rigging lines like Stable Braid, and accessory products like Zing-It throw line.

Pick a climbing line based on your hitch or device, your preferred handling and the manufacturer's compatibility guidance. For rigging, size the rope well beyond expected loads to allow for shock loading. Inspect rope often and retire it when it is damaged.

name: Sawpod
title: Sawpod Chainsaw Accessories
meta: Sawpod chainsaw accessories for tree crews and saw users. See the Sawpod items we list, with plain notes on what each one does and how it fits on the job.
intro: Sawpod is a brand of chainsaw accessories. This page collects the Sawpod items we list, with straightforward notes on each one.
about: We focus on the products and how they get used. Each Sawpod listing explains what the item does and where it fits in a saw kit.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions, and make sure any accessory is compatible with your saw before you use it.

name: Sena
title: Sena Tufftalk Headsets for Tree Crews
meta: Sena Tufftalk headsets combine hearing protection with Bluetooth mesh communication, letting tree crews talk between the climber and the ground crew.
intro: Sena makes Bluetooth communication headsets, including the Tufftalk earmuff line built for loud jobsites. Sena Tufftalk lets a climber and ground crew talk without shouting over saws and chippers.
about: Communication between the climber and the ground is one of the biggest safety factors in tree work. Sena Tufftalk headsets combine earmuff hearing protection with intercom communication, so crews can coordinate cuts, rigging and lowering without hand signals alone.

The Tufftalk Lite is a lighter version, and Sena sells replacement parts like ear cushions. Agree on clear commands and a backup plan if the radios fail, and keep your hearing protection in good condition.

name: Silky
title: Silky Saws: Zubat, Sugoi, Gomtaro & More
meta: Silky saws from Japan for arborists: the Zubat, Sugoi, Gomtaro, Tsurugi and Gunfighter. Compare Silky pruning saws and blades for climbing and ground work.
intro: Silky is the Japanese saw maker behind many of the hand saws arborists carry. A Silky arborist saw like the Zubat or Sugoi is often the first pruning saw a climber buys.
about: Silky saws use hard, sharp, pull-stroke blades that cut fast and leave clean finish cuts. The line includes curved saws like the Zubat, Sugoi and Tsurugi, straight saws like the Gomtaro, and folding saws like the Pocketboy, in many lengths and tooth patterns.

Replacement blades are available for many models, so you can keep a handle and scabbard and swap the blade as it dulls. Store your saw in its scabbard, clip it to your saddle with a lanyard when climbing, and keep hands clear of the cutting path.

name: Simonds
title: Simonds Files & Cutting Tools
meta: Simonds files and cutting tools for saw sharpening and shop work. Learn how Simonds files fit into keeping chainsaw chain and hand tools sharp.
intro: Simonds International is known for files and industrial cutting tools. Simonds files help crews keep chain and tools sharp.
about: Simonds has a long history in industrial cutting tools and files. For tree crews, the files are the main draw: round files for chain sharpening and flat files for depth gauges and tool maintenance.
Use the correct file size for your chain, keep files clean and dry, and replace them once they stop biting.

name: SMC
title: SMC Pulleys & Carabiners
meta: SMC pulleys, carabiners and rescue hardware for arborists. Compare SMC pulleys like the CRx and steel locking carabiners for climbing and rigging setups.
intro: SMC makes rescue and rope access hardware including pulleys and carabiners. SMC pulleys and steel carabiners show up in arborist climbing and rigging kits.
about: SMC hardware comes from the rescue world, where gear has to be tough and dependable. Arborists use SMC pulleys, such as the CRx, in climbing systems and haul setups, and SMC steel locking carabiners where extra strength and wear resistance matter.
Choose pulleys sized for your rope, check ratings, and inspect sheaves and side plates for wear. Retire hardware that has been dropped hard or shows cracks.

name: Stein
title: Stein Arborist Rigging & Climbing Gear
meta: Stein arborist gear for rigging and climbing: slings, rigging hardware, lanyards and accessories for tree crews. Plain notes on each Stein item we list.
intro: Stein makes arborist climbing and rigging gear. Stein gear covers slings, rigging accessories and climbing equipment used by tree crews.
about: Stein's range is aimed squarely at tree work, from rigging slings and hardware to climbing accessories. It suits crews looking to fill out a rigging kit with gear made for arborist use.
Size rigging gear for the loads you expect, including shock loads, and follow the manufacturer's working load guidance. Inspect slings and hardware before every job.

name: Sterling Rope
title: Sterling Rope: HTP Static, WorkPro & PAS
meta: Sterling rope for arborists, including HTP static and WorkPro climbing lines, the Sterling PAS and rope by the foot for lanyards, prusiks and accessories.
intro: Sterling Rope is a US maker of climbing and work ropes. Sterling rope like HTP Static and WorkPro is popular with SRS climbers who want a firm, low-stretch line.
about: Sterling makes ropes for climbing, rescue and work at height. Static lines like HTP and WorkPro are common SRS choices in tree work, and Sterling also makes accessory cord, slings and the PAS, a personal anchor system built from a chain of sewn loops.

Rope by the foot is handy for lanyards, prusiks and accessory lines. Make sure any rope or cord used for life support is rated for that purpose and compatible with your devices, and inspect it before every climb.

name: Teufelberger
title: Teufelberger Climbing Rope: Safety Blue & More
meta: Teufelberger climbing rope from Austria for arborists, including Safety Blue, Ultra-Vee and other lines for MRS and SRS climbing, plus rigging rope.
intro: Teufelberger is an Austrian rope maker with a long line of arborist ropes. Teufelberger climbing lines like Safety Blue and Ultra-Vee have been in tree climbers' bags for years.
about: Teufelberger makes climbing and rigging ropes in a range of constructions, from classic 16-strand lines suited to friction hitches to firmer ropes for SRS and mechanical devices. Safety Blue and Ultra-Vee are two of the most familiar names.

Teufelberger also makes rigging lines and accessory cord. Pick a climbing rope that is compatible with your hitch or device, follow the manufacturer's guidance, and retire rope that is cut, glazed or shock-loaded.

name: Weaver
title: Weaver Arborist Saddles, Chest Box & Gear
meta: Weaver arborist gear: climbing saddles, the chest box, chainsaw straps, logging belts, throw bags and leather goods built for tree and utility crews.
intro: Weaver Leather is a US company that makes climbing saddles, chest harnesses and tool accessories for tree workers. Weaver arborist gear is known for practical, durable designs.
about: Weaver started in leather and now makes a full line of arborist and utility gear. That includes climbing saddles, the chest box for chest harness setups, chainsaw straps, logging belts and throw bags.

Weaver gear tends to suit crews who want simple, tough equipment at a fair price. As with any saddle or harness, follow the instructions, check stitching and hardware before each climb, and retire gear that is worn or damaged.

name: Wesco
title: Wesco Lineman Boots & Highliner Climbing Boots
meta: Wesco lineman boots and Highliner climbing boots for spur climbers. Handmade US leather boots with stiff shanks for long days on spurs and on the ground.
intro: Wesco makes handmade leather boots in the US. Wesco lineman boots like the Highliner are a favorite of climbers who spend long days on spurs.
about: Spur climbing puts a lot of pressure on the arch of your foot. Wesco lineman and climbing boots are built with stiff shanks and heavy leather to support that, and the Highliner is one of the best-known models for climbers.
Good boots last for years with care and can often be rebuilt. Break them in before a long climb, keep the leather conditioned, and replace or resole when the support starts to go.

name: West Coast Saw
title: West Coast Saw Chainsaw Parts & Gear
meta: West Coast Saw chainsaw parts, chain, bars and accessories for tree crews and woodcutters. See the West Coast Saw items we list with practical notes.
intro: West Coast Saw is a name tree crews and woodcutters know from chainsaw parts and gear. This page collects the West Coast Saw items we list.
about: We keep this page focused on the products. Each West Coast Saw listing explains what the item is for, which saws or setups it fits, and what to check before you buy.
When buying chain, bars or parts, confirm the fit with your saw's model and manual. Match chain pitch, gauge and drive link count to the bar, and keep parts and tools clean and in good repair.

name: Yale Cordage
title: Yale Cordage: Yale Grips, Maxijacket & Rope
meta: Yale Cordage rope and accessories for arborists and utility crews, including Yale Grips, Maxijacket rigging rope and climbing lines from the Maine rope maker.
intro: Yale Cordage is a rope maker based in Maine. Arborists know Yale Cordage for climbing and rigging ropes, Maxijacket rope, and Yale Grips for gripping rope and cable.
about: Yale makes rope for utility, industrial and tree care work. Maxijacket is one of its rigging lines, and Yale climbing ropes are also used by arborists. Yale Grips are woven grips that slide onto a line and tighten under load.
Size rigging rope for the loads you expect, including shock loads, and follow the manufacturer's guidance. Inspect rope and grips often, and retire anything that is damaged.

name: Husqvarna
title: Husqvarna Chainsaws, Top-Handles & Gear
meta: Husqvarna chainsaws and gear for tree work: the 372XP, 572XP, 550XP, T540XP top-handle, battery saws, chaps, helmets and parts for arborists.
intro: Husqvarna is a Swedish power equipment maker whose chainsaws are found on tree crews everywhere. Husqvarna chainsaws like the 372XP, 572XP and T540XP top-handle are workhorses for felling, bucking and climbing.
about: Husqvarna's XP line is built for professionals who run saws all day. Mid-size saws like the 550XP and 562XP handle limbing and bucking, the 372XP and 572XP are classic 70 cc removal saws, and big saws like the 395XP and 592XP pull long bars on large wood. The T540XP top-handle is a common climbing saw, and Husqvarna also makes battery saws for in-tree and noise-sensitive work.

Beyond saws, Husqvarna makes bars, chain, fuel and oil, helmets, chaps, gloves, axes and log tools. Read the operator's manual, use the correct bar and chain combinations, wear full PPE, and get training for felling and climbing saw use. Top-handle saws are designed for trained arborists working in trees.

name: NGK
title: NGK Spark Plugs for Chainsaws
meta: NGK spark plugs for chainsaws and small engines, including the BPMR7A and CMR6H. Learn how to match the right NGK plug to your saw and check the gap.
intro: NGK is a Japanese spark plug maker whose plugs are used in many chainsaws and small engines. NGK spark plugs like the BPMR7A and CMR6H are common replacements for professional saws.
about: A fresh plug is one of the cheapest fixes for a saw that is hard to start or running rough. NGK makes plugs in many sizes and heat ranges, and the code on each plug tells you its thread size, design, resistor type and heat range, so plugs are not interchangeable just because they look similar.
Always confirm the right plug in your saw's operator's manual, check the gap before installing, and read the old plug's color for clues about how your saw is running.

name: Clogger
title: Clogger Chainsaw Pants & Chaps
meta: Clogger chainsaw pants and chaps built to be light and cool, including the Zero, DefenderPro and denim chainsaw pants, plus apron-style chaps.
intro: Clogger makes chainsaw protective clothing with a focus on light weight and breathability. Clogger chainsaw pants like the Zero line are popular with arborists who wear protection all day.
about: Heavy, hot chainsaw protection gets left in the truck. Clogger builds pants and chaps designed to be light and cool enough that you will actually wear them. The Zero line is aimed at hot weather and climbing, the DefenderPro is a tougher option, and denim chainsaw pants look like regular work pants.

Apron-style chaps from Clogger are an option for ground work. Check the protection standard on the label against what your employer and the applicable rules require, and retire any protective garment that has been cut.

name: CMI
title: CMI Rescue & Climbing Hardware
meta: CMI climbing and rescue hardware for arborists: anchor slings, pulleys, carabiners and rope grabs. Tough rescue-world gear for tree climbing and rigging.
intro: CMI makes climbing and rescue hardware including anchor slings, pulleys and carabiners. Arborists use CMI gear for anchors and climbing setups.
about: CMI builds gear with roots in rescue work, where hardware has to be simple and tough. For tree work, CMI anchor slings are a common way to set a basal or canopy anchor, and their pulleys and rope grabs fit into climbing and haul systems.
Check ratings and rope compatibility for every piece, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and inspect slings and hardware before every use.
